provenance.what: Rule-learner baselines for the paper's tab:rule_learners. PAPER NUMBERS.
provenance.units: 28 (knowledge base, sampling) units -- every unit with an acquisition result. busybox RS(2n)/RS(3n) are absent because no acquisition run exists there; a baseline cell beside an absent ConGen cell compares against nothing.
provenance.folds: the same committed folds the acquisition sweep used (data/folds/)
provenance.scorer: the corrected scorer: each fold scored against its own oracle
provenance.reporting_rule: a cell is scored only when BOTH classes have >= 10 training instances; otherwise it is marked too_few_instances and NOT scored. Declared before any number existed.
provenance.tiers: accuracy + semantic only. The description tier is omitted by design: a rule set carries no bias constraint names, so its description F1 is ~0 by construction and printing it would be a straw man.
provenance.semantic_caveat: LEAD WITH RECALL. Recall shares its denominator (the target theory's clauses) with the acquisition side and is comparable. PRECISION IS NOT: ConGen counts CNF clauses per learned constraint, a rule set counts one clause per rule. F1 inherits this. Build no claim on a precision difference between the sides.
